principles: Only formal, fresh, gate-consumed evidence can unlock Layer 2.
Layer 2 evidence must not imply Loop, Production, or global claim unlock.
Implementation must fit existing baseline and Authority boundaries without a parallel framework.
drivers: The user wants Layer 2 formally unlocked only after all gate/proof/suite/claim checks pass.
Existing code already contains baseline definitions and fail-closed suite logic, so the real gap is formal proof production and consumption.
Authority receipt binding is required to prevent local text or stale artifacts from becoming capability proof.
Higher-layer claims must remain locked to avoid false capability claims.

options.name: A: Extend existing baseline suite with formal Layer 2 proof consumption
pros: Uses current ENG baseline registry, suite report, and claim evaluator concepts.
Keeps implementation narrow around real correctness gaps.
Maintains fail-closed behavior for diagnostic artifacts and higher layers.
cons: Requires careful tests around receipt binding, lower-layer proof, and stale materialHash.
May need small command-policy/process-fact updates so formal and diagnostic surfaces are not confused.

options.name: B: Create a separate Layer 2 unlock framework
pros: Could isolate formal unlock behavior from existing diagnostic commands.
Might be easier to explain as a new command surface.
cons: Adds parallel schema and gate concepts without proving existing ones insufficient.
Higher risk of inconsistency with current baseline_suite_report and capability_claim_evaluate behavior.

options.name: C: Treat current diagnostic baseline reports as sufficient
cons: Incorrect: current reports are localOnly=true and capabilityProof=false.
Violates the decision document and creates a false capability claim.

chosen: A: Extend existing baseline suite with formal Layer 2 proof consumption
rationale: Option A fixes the actual correctness gap while preserving the existing architecture. It lets diagnostic commands remain diagnostic, requires fresh formal proof before PASS, and keeps higher-layer claims locked. Option B adds avoidable framework surface, and Option C would be a false unlock.

preMortem.scenario: Diagnostic artifacts are accidentally accepted as formal Engineering proof.
preMortem.trigger: Suite aggregation checks only outcome=PASS and ignores localOnly/capabilityProof.
preMortem.consequence: Layer 2 appears unlocked without Authority-backed proof.
preMortem.mitigation: Add or preserve tests that reject localOnly=true, capabilityProof=false, and stale materialHash artifacts.

preMortem.scenario: Authority receipt does not bind the actual baseline or claim target.
preMortem.trigger: Receipt ref is verified generally but baselineId, suiteRunId, claimTarget, or materialHash are not checked.
preMortem.consequence: A valid receipt from another run can unlock the wrong claim.
preMortem.mitigation: Require canonical binding fields in formal reports and fail closed on missing or mismatched binding.

preMortem.scenario: Layer 2 unlock leaks into Loop Engineering or Production Safety claims.
preMortem.trigger: Claim evaluator maps Engineering PASS to broader authorizedClaimLevel.
preMortem.consequence: The system overclaims unattended or production-grade capability.
preMortem.mitigation: Test higher-layer requests remain not_authorized unless their own lower-layer and safety proofs exist.

preMortem.scenario: Implementation creates a new unlock path that lifecycle gates do not consume.
preMortem.trigger: Formal reports are written but not read by suite/claim/gate logic.
preMortem.consequence: The story reports success but no actual gate can enforce it.
preMortem.mitigation: Require tests that the formal suite report and claim evaluator consume the produced artifacts and reject malformed/stale variants.
